source_text: Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη ἐν ἀνθρώποις ⸀εὐδοκίας.
english_snapshot: Glory to God in the highest[c][b][a], and on earth peace among people of good pleasure.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'and on earth peace, good will among men.'

source_text: Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως, ἀνήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παραστῆσαι τῷ κυρίῳ,
english_snapshot: And when the days of their purification were fulfilled according to the law of Moses[a], they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'her purification' instead of 'their purification.'

source_text: τοῦ Συμεὼν τοῦ Ἰούδα τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τοῦ Ἰωνὰμ τοῦ Ἐλιακὶμ
english_snapshot: the son of Simeon[a], the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim[b],

signals.text: Some manuscripts or translation traditions reflect the name as 'Jonan' rather than 'Jonam.'

source_text: τοῦ Μελεὰ τοῦ Μεννὰ τοῦ Ματταθὰ τοῦ Ναθὰμ τοῦ Δαυὶδ
english_snapshot: the son of Melea[a], the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David[b],

signals.text: Some English versions have 'Menan' instead of 'Menna,' reflecting a different form of the name; the SBLGNT text here reads 'Menna.'

source_text: τοῦ ⸂Ἀμιναδὰβ τοῦ Ἀδμὶν τοῦ Ἀρνὶ⸃ τοῦ Ἑσρὼμ τοῦ Φαρὲς τοῦ Ἰούδα
english_snapshot: the son of Amminadab[a], the son of Admin, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the son of Amminadab, the son of Admin, the son of Aram,' while others omit 'Admin' and read 'the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram.'

source_text: τοῦ Καϊνὰμ τοῦ Ἀρφαξὰδ τοῦ Σὴμ τοῦ Νῶε τοῦ Λάμεχ
english_snapshot: the son of Cainan[a], the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech[c][b],

signals.text: Some traditions omit Cainan here in order to align the genealogy more closely with certain Old Testament forms.

source_text: καὶ ἦν κηρύσσων ⸂εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς⸃ τῆς ⸀Ἰουδαίας.
english_snapshot: And he was preaching in the synagogues of Judea[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Galilee' instead of 'Judea.' The main text follows the reading 'Judea' in the Greek text used here.

source_text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· καὶ δύναμις κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι ⸀αὐτόν.
english_snapshot: And it happened on one of those days that he was teaching[a], and Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there, who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem; and the power of the Lord was there for him to heal.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'to heal them' instead of 'for him to heal.'

source_text: ⸀καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν ⸀παλαιὸν θέλει νέον· λέγει γάρ· Ὁ παλαιὸς ⸀χρηστός ἐστιν.
english_snapshot: And no one[a], after drinking old wine, wants new, for he says, ‘The old is good.’

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'The old is better.'

source_text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ⸀ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν, καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς.
english_snapshot: And it happened on the next day that he went into a town called Nain[a], and his disciples and a large crowd were going with him.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'soon afterward' instead of 'on the next day.'

source_text: καὶ Ἰωάννα γυνὴ Χουζᾶ ἐπιτρόπου Ἡρῴδου καὶ Σουσάννα καὶ ἕτεραι πολλαί, αἵτινες διηκόνουν αὐτοῖς ⸀ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐταῖς.
english_snapshot: and Joanna[a], the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others[b], who were serving them out of their possessions.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “him” instead of “them.”

source_text: Καὶ κατέπλευσαν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν ⸀Γερασηνῶν, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἀντιπέρα τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
english_snapshot: And they sailed down to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and parallel Gospel passages read 'Gadarenes' or 'Gergesenes.'

source_text: ἐξῆλθον δὲ ἰδεῖν τὸ γεγονὸς καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ εὗρον καθήμενον τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀφ’ οὗ τὰ δαιμόνια ⸀ἐξῆλθεν ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.
english_snapshot: Then they went out to see what had happened[a], and they came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting, clothed, and in his right mind at Jesus's feet[b], and they were afraid.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read the verb as plural ('the demons had gone out'); the printed text has a singular verb with a plural subject, but the sense is unchanged.

source_text: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος ἀπὸ ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἥτις ⸂ἰατροῖς προσαναλώσασα ὅλον τὸν βίον⸃ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ⸀ἀπ’ οὐδενὸς θεραπευθῆναι,
english_snapshot: And a woman who had been in a flow of blood for twelve years[a], and who had spent her whole livelihood on physicians, was not able to be healed by anyone[c][b],

signals.text: Some manuscripts, reflected in the Textus Receptus and thus the KJV tradition, add that she 'could not be healed by any' after stating that she had spent all her livelihood on physicians; the SBLGNT text includes the inability clause but not the stronger implication that the physicians failed her by explicit addition beyond this wording.

source_text: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ⸀ἐκλελεγμένος, αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε.
english_snapshot: And a voice came from the cloud[a], saying, “This is my Son, the Chosen One; listen to him.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'my beloved Son' instead of 'my Son, my Chosen One.'

source_text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ἀγγέλους πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ. καὶ πορευθέντες εἰσῆλθον εἰς κώμην Σαμαριτῶν, ⸀ὡς ἑτοιμάσαι αὐτῷ·
english_snapshot: And he sent messengers ahead of him[b][a]. And they went and entered a village of the Samaritans to prepare for him.

signals.text: Or 'a Samaritan village.' The Greek more literally says 'a village of the Samaritans.'

source_text: στραφεὶς δὲ ἐπετίμησεν ⸀αὐτοῖς.
english_snapshot: But he turned and rebuked them[a].

signals.text: Some later manuscripts add: 'and said, “You do not know what sort of spirit you are of; for the Son of Man did not come to destroy people's lives but to save them.”'

source_text: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ κύριος ⸀καὶ ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα ⸀δύο καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο ⸁δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι.
english_snapshot: After these things[a], the Lord appointed seventy-two others also, and sent them two by two ahead of him into every town and place where he himself was about to go.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'seventy' instead of 'seventy-two.'

source_text: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα ⸀δύο μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες· Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου.
english_snapshot: Then the seventy-two returned with joy[a], saying, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “the seventy” instead of “the seventy-two.”

source_text: καὶ τῇδε ἦν ἀδελφὴ καλουμένη ⸀Μαριάμ, ἣ καὶ ⸂παρακαθεσθεῖσα πρὸς⸃ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ ⸀Ἰησοῦ ἤκουεν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ.
english_snapshot: And she had a sister called Mary[a], who also sat at Jesus’ feet and was listening to his word.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Jesus' instead of 'the Lord.'

source_text: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν ⸀αὐτοῦ, καὶ ⸀ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
english_snapshot: But seek his kingdom[b][a], and these things will be added to you.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the kingdom of God' instead of 'his kingdom.'

source_text: ⸀καὶ πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· Τίνος ὑμῶν υἱὸς ἢ βοῦς εἰς φρέαρ ⸀πεσεῖται, καὶ οὐκ εὐθέως ἀνασπάσει αὐτὸν ⸀ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;
english_snapshot: And he said to them[a], “Which of you, if a son or an ox falls into a well, will not immediately pull him out on the Sabbath day?”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “donkey” instead of “son.”

source_text: εἶπεν δὲ ⸂ὁ υἱὸς αὐτῷ⸃· Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου, ⸀οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός ⸀σου.
english_snapshot: But the son said to him[a], ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you[b]. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

signals.text: Some manuscripts continue the son's speech with words equivalent to 'Treat me as one of your hired servants,' harmonizing with v. 19; the SBLGNT text ends the sentence at 'your son.'

source_text: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς. ἐὰν ⸀ἁμάρτῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἐπιτίμησον αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐὰν μετανοήσῃ ἄφες αὐτῷ·
english_snapshot: Pay attention to yourselves[a]. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents[b], forgive him.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'If your brother sins against you, rebuke him.'

source_text: Δύο ἔσονται ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ· εἷς παραληφθήσεται, καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἀφεθήσεται.
english_snapshot: Two[a] men will be in the field; one will be taken, and the other will be left.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations, but is present in the Western tradition (such as the 5th-century Codex Bezae), the Byzantine majority tradition, and the Latin Vulgate. It was likely added by later scribes to harmonize with Matthew 24:40.

source_text: ὅτι δὲ ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροὶ καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἐμήνυσεν ἐπὶ τῆς βάτου, ὡς λέγει κύριον τὸν θεὸν Ἀβραὰμ ⸀καὶ θεὸν Ἰσαὰκ ⸁καὶ θεὸν Ἰακώβ·
english_snapshot: But that the dead are raised[a], even Moses made known in the passage about the bush[b], where he calls the Lord the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.

signals.text: Greek 'the Lord'; this reflects the Septuagint's customary rendering of the divine name in Exodus 3.

source_text: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν ⸀κτήσασθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
english_snapshot: By your endurance you will gain your lives[a][b].

signals.text: Or, more formally, 'In your endurance, gain your lives,' reflecting the imperative form of the verb.

source_text: ἀγρυπνεῖτε ⸀δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα ⸀κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ⸀ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
english_snapshot: But stay awake at all times[a], praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to happen[c][b], and to stand before the Son of Man.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things...' instead of 'that you may have strength to escape all these things...'

source_text: καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου ⸂[τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν διδόμενον· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
english_snapshot: And taking bread[a], after giving thanks he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you[c][b]. Keep doing this in remembrance of me.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit: 'which is given for you. Keep doing this in remembrance of me.'

source_text: ⸂ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος ⸀ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ ἐνισχύων αὐτόν.
english_snapshot: Then an angel from heaven appeared to him[a], strengthening him.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit verses 43–44.

source_text: καὶ γενόμενος ἐν ἀγωνίᾳ ἐκτενέστερον προσηύχετο· ⸄καὶ ἐγένετο⸅ ὁ ἱδρὼς αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ θρόμβοι αἵματος καταβαίνοντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.⸃
english_snapshot: And being in agony[a], he was praying more intensely[c][b]; and his sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit Luke 22:43–44; others include them. The SBLGNT prints the verses in brackets to reflect this textual uncertainty.

source_text: Ἀνάγκην δὲ εἶχεν ἀπολύειν αὐτοῖς κατὰ ἑορτὴν ἕνα.
english_snapshot: He had an obligation[a] to release one man to them at the festival.

signals.text: This entire verse is absent from several of the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 3rd-century Papyrus 75 and 4th-century Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations. It is present in other major early manuscripts (such as the 4th-century Sinaiticus), the Latin tradition, and the later Byzantine majority. It was likely added by scribes to harmonize Luke's account with the release custom mentioned in Matthew 27:15 and Mark 15:6. Some manuscripts place this sentence after verse 18.

source_text: ⸂ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν· Πάτερ, ἄφες αὐτοῖς, οὐ γὰρ οἴδασιν τί ποιοῦσιν.⸃ διαμεριζόμενοι δὲ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἔβαλον ⸀κλήρους.
english_snapshot: But Jesus was saying[a], “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And dividing his garments, they cast lots.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit: “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”

source_text: καὶ ⸀ἔλεγεν· Ἰησοῦ, μνήσθητί ⸀μου ὅταν ἔλθῃς ⸂ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ⸃ σου.
english_snapshot: And he said[a], “Jesus, remember me when you come in your kingdom.”

signals.text: Or “when you come in your kingdom.” Some manuscripts read “into your kingdom” more explicitly, while the SBLGNT text reads “in your kingdom.”

source_text: ⸂εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ⸃ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ ⸀σῶμα.
english_snapshot: But when they entered[a], they did not find the body.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'the body of the Lord Jesus.'

source_text: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτῶν λαλούντων ⸀αὐτὸς ἔστη ἐν μέσῳ ⸀αὐτῶν.
english_snapshot: While they were saying these things[a], he himself stood among them.

signals.text: Some manuscripts add, 'and he says to them, “Peace to you.”'

source_text: ⸂[καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ⸀ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας.]⸃
english_snapshot: And after saying this[a], he showed them his hands and his feet.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit this sentence.

source_text: οἱ δὲ ἐπέδωκαν αὐτῷ ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ ⸀μέρος·
english_snapshot: And they gave him a piece of broiled fish[a].

signals.text: Some later manuscripts add, 'and from a honeycomb.'

source_text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εὐλογεῖν αὐτὸν αὐτοὺς διέστη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ⸂[καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν]⸃.
english_snapshot: And it happened that[a], while he was blessing them, he parted from them and was carried up into heaven.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit 'and was carried up into heaven.'

source_text: καὶ αὐτοὶ ⸂[προσκυνήσαντες αὐτὸν]⸃ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ μετὰ χαρᾶς μεγάλης,
english_snapshot: And they[a], after worshiping him, returned to Jerusalem with great joy[b],

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit 'after worshiping him.'
